title: How robots move and sense
examples: How does a robot know where it is?
What part tells the robot what to do?
Can robots feel things like we do?

explain.say: Today we learn how robots move and sense their world. We look at the parts that make robots work.
Sensors are like the robot's five senses. They collect information about the environment around it.

items: Tactile sensors detect touch and pressure.

explain.say: Motors provide the power to make the robot move. They convert electrical energy into motion.
The controller acts as the robot's brain. It processes the sensor data and sends commands to the motors.
Joints allow robots to move in specific ways. They connect parts and limit the robot's movement range.
Feedback is crucial for accuracy. It allows the robot to check if its action was correct.

faq.q: Do robots need batteries to move?
faq.a: Yes, motors require an electrical power source, usually batteries or a power supply. This energy makes the motors turn.
asks: Where does the energy for movement come from?

faq.q: How do sensors know what they are sensing?
faq.a: Different sensors are designed for specific things, like measuring distance or detecting heat. They convert physical changes into electrical signals.
asks: What is the job of a sensor?

faq.q: Is the controller always the part that thinks?
faq.a: The controller, often a computer or microchip, processes all the information. It decides what the robot should do next based on the inputs.
asks: Which part is the robot's brain?

faq.q: What is the difference between a joint and a motor?
faq.a: The motor provides the force to move, while the joint is the physical connection that limits the direction of that movement. The motor drives the joint.
asks: Does the motor move the joint?
What is the physical connection point?

faq.q: What happens if the feedback system fails?
faq.a: If feedback fails, the robot might think it has reached a target when it has not. It will continue moving incorrectly because it cannot check its own position.
asks: Why is feedback important for movement?

facts: Sensors measure physical quantities like distance or light intensity.
Motors convert electrical energy into mechanical motion.
The controller processes data from sensors to send commands to motors.
Joints restrict movement to specific axes, like bending an elbow.

quiz.say: If a robot arm needs to bend at the elbow, what part limits that specific movement?
quiz.why: Joints are the mechanical points that define how far and in what direction a limb can move.

wrong.0: Sensors only detect information; they cannot physically limit movement.
wrong.1: The controller sends the signal, but the joint is the physical mechanism that stops it.
wrong.3: Motors provide the power to bend, but the joint defines the physical limit.

quiz.say: A robot moves forward, detects it is too close to a wall, and stops. Which concept describes the robot checking its position?
quiz.why: Feedback is the process where the robot checks its actual result against its goal to make corrections.

wrong.0: The controller makes the decision, but feedback is the specific loop of checking that decision.
wrong.2: Sensors only report the data; feedback is the use of that data to correct action.
wrong.3: Motors are the output; they are what cause the movement, not the check.
